references.text: God makes the covenant with Israel at Sinai (Horeb), which is mentioned as the former covenant in Deuteronomy 29:1.
Moses sprinkles the blood of the covenant on the people at Sinai, which is the covenant made at Horeb.
The Lord commands Moses to write the words of the covenant, corresponding to the commission given in the land of Moab.
Refers to the covenant at Horeb with the Ten Commandments, which is the former covenant mentioned in the verse.
Moses reminds the people of the covenant the Lord made with them at Horeb.
The continuation of the covenant renewal in the land of Moab introduced in 29:1.
Joshua renews the covenant with the people, in line with the tradition of covenant renewal that Moses began.
Solomon mentions the covenant at Horeb when Israel left Egypt, the same covenant mentioned in Deuteronomy 29:1.
Jeremiah prophesies about a new covenant that will be different from the covenant God made when He brought the people out of Egypt.
The book of Hebrews quotes Jeremiah regarding the new covenant that is to replace the old covenant from Sinai/Horeb.
Refers to the first covenant that was inaugurated with blood, corresponding to the covenant at Horeb.
